entries.clue: Liberal spreading often a good thing for soil (5)

indicatorNotes.spreading: MUCH spreads itself out wide enough to take L inside

blocks.note: much = often, as in 'do you go there much?'

annotation.surface: A gardener's tip that spreading something liberally is often good for the soil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liberal spreading' reads as generous application; in fact Liberal is only the letter L, and it is 'often' that does the spreading.
annotation.definitionFit: Mulch is a layer of bark, compost or straw spread on soil to feed it and keep in moisture.

entries.clue: Student changing into top from M&S makes promiscuous one horny (5)

indicatorNotes.changing into: the L is swapped for another letter

blocks.note: loose = promiscuous, in the old-fashioned sense
L = learner, the letter on a learner driver's plate
the first letter of Marks and Spencer, a British department store

annotation.surface: A saucy line about a student who changes into a top bought at Marks & Spencer and becomes irresistible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horny' is the joke: a moose has horns, or antlers, so it is 'one horny'. 'Changing into top' looks like getting dressed but is an instruction to swap L for M.
annotation.definitionFit: A moose carries huge antlers, so it is literally a horned, 'horny' creature.

entries.clue: Shut, leaderless, small cafe sadly suffers blow to reputation (5,4)

indicatorNotes.leaderless: the word loses its first letter, its leader
indicatorNotes.sadly: CAFE is upset, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A small cafe has sadly shut, and its good name has taken a knock.
annotation.definitionFit: To lose face is to be humiliated, to suffer a loss of respect or standing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shut' wants to be the definition of a closed cafe; the definition is the idiom at the end, and 'sadly' only stirs CAFE.

entries.clue: The Mrs and I disturbed people seeking peace and quiet (7)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: the letters are shaken out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A husband complains that he and his wife were disturbed by people who just wanted peace and quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Mrs' looks like a phrase to translate as WIFE or HER; here its letters are used exactly as printed, with 'and' only joining them to I.
annotation.definitionFit: Hermits withdraw from society to live alone in peace and quiet.

entries.clue: Reason to limit beer consumption (9)

annotation.surface: Someone wants a good reason before they cut back on their drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a single thought about drinking less; the break comes straight after 'Reason'.
annotation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reason or logic behind something.

entries.clue: Trump experienced this therapy, one with electric charge, following stumble (2-8)

indicatorNotes.following: the other pieces come after REEL

blocks.note: to reel = to stagger or stumble
a switched-on circuit is live, carrying a charge

annotation.surface: A dig suggesting Trump was once given electric shock treatment after a fall.
annotation.walkthrough: The electrical words all point toward shock treatment, which is half right: ECT is the therapy, but the definition is the opening phrase, and in 2024 Trump won a second term.
annotation.definitionFit: Donald Trump was elected again in 2024, a re-election after his first term.

entries.clue: Slice of toast or not? Struggling to decide (4)

indicatorNotes.Slice of: the answer is a thin slice cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the three words, starting at the last letter of toast

annotation.surface: A breakfast dilemma: have a slice of toast or not?
annotation.walkthrough: The question in the middle of the clue is itself the dilemma the definition describes.
annotation.definitionFit: To be torn is to be pulled between two choices and unable to decide.

entries.clue: Folding love note after a doctor visits (7)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' puts the note behind the A, so it follows it in the answer
indicatorNotes.visits: RIG goes in, as a visitor goes into a house

blocks.note: O = love, the zero score in tennis
to doctor = to rig, tamper with
mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A love note is folded up after the doctor calls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' wants to be DR or MO; here it is a verb, meaning to tamper, which gives RIG to slip between O and AMI.
annotation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

entries.clue: Muppet Movie's selling point perhaps (5)

blocks.note: a muppet is British slang for a fool, an ass

annotation.surface: A marketing question: what is The Muppet Movie's big selling point?
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Muppet Movie' one title, but the two words work separately. In Britain 'muppet' is everyday slang for an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: A selling point is an asset, something in a product's favour; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

entries.clue: European organisation hosts jolly for all (9)

indicatorNotes.hosts: the organisation takes the other word in, as a host takes in guests

annotation.surface: A European organisation throws a jolly, a fun outing, open to all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' reads as a noun, a party; it is the adverb meaning very. E and BODY together form the host.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'all' used as a pronoun, as in 'all were welcome', means every person.

entries.clue: Participate in part of rally led by former student (7)

indicatorNotes.led by: whatever is led by someone has that person walking at its head, so OB comes first

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
a tennis rally starts with the serve

annotation.surface: A former student leads part of a political rally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rally' suggests a march or a car race; it is the tennis sense, where the serve opens each exchange.
annotation.definitionFit: To observe a custom or festival is to take part in it, as in observing Lent.

entries.clue: Division of Nature is sued for unoriginal publication (7)

indicatorNotes.Division of: a section is cut out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the words, from the tail of Nature through 'is' into the start of sued

annotation.surface: A division of the journal Nature is taken to court over publishing something that was not new.
annotation.walkthrough: Nature is a leading science journal, so the lawsuit over an unoriginal paper sounds real.
annotation.definitionFit: A reissue is something published again, so not an original edition.

entries.clue: Adjoining areas where hundreds and thousands might be gathered? (2,6)

blocks.clueFragment: where hundreds and thousands might be gathered
blocks.note: hundreds and thousands are tiny sugar sprinkles, found in sweets

annotation.surface: A riddle about which rooms are big enough to gather hundreds and thousands of people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hundreds and thousands' look like crowds; in Britain they are tiny coloured sugar sprinkles for cakes. Where are they gathered? 'In sweets', said out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom joined directly onto a bedroom.

entries.clue: Store mostly underwear in front of vacant repository (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: 'mostly' means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.vacant: empty the word of its insides, leaving its outer letters

annotation.surface: A note about keeping most of your underwear in an empty storage unit.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pants' are underwear, not trousers.
annotation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room for storing food.

entries.clue: Loud blow to indicate the start of hostilities? (10)

blocks.note: a lash = a stroke of a whip

annotation.surface: A loud blow, like a gunshot, signals that fighting has begun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loud blow' reads as one noisy explosion; it splits into F and LASH.
annotation.definitionFit: A flashpoint is the moment or place where conflict breaks out.

entries.clue: Carmaker's headquarters (5)

blocks.note: belonging to the Spanish car company SEAT; the apostrophe is the possessive
a seat = the base of a company or government

annotation.surface: Just a label: a car company's head office.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase; the apostrophe lets SEAT'S stand on its own, and 'headquarters' is the second meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: A seat is where power sits, as in the seat of government; SEAT is also the Spanish carmaker.

entries.clue: South American king provided crystal meth for prostitute (9)

blocks.note: CR = Carolus Rex, King Charles's royal cipher
ice is slang for crystal meth

annotation.surface: A South American drug lord supplies crystal meth to a sex worker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prostitute' looks like a noun but is the verb: to prostitute your talents is to sell them out, to sacrifice them.
annotation.definitionFit: To prostitute something is to give it up cheaply for gain, which is to sacrifice it.

entries.clue: Approaching on foot, women off for term's opening lecture (7,2)

indicatorNotes.off: something that is off has gone, so the W leaves the phrase
indicatorNotes.for: 'for' as in 'in exchange for': T is put in place of the departed W

annotation.surface: A lecturer walks in to give the first lecture of term, with the women absent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' is the definition in its telling-off sense, not the academic one the surface paints.
annotation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding, a lecture about bad behaviour.

entries.clue: Bits of information on European country written by local (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, GEN sits on top of the rest

blocks.note: Italy as the Italians themselves write it

annotation.surface: Snippets of information about a European country, written by someone who lives there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bits of information' reads as one phrase; 'bits' is on its own, the coy slang for private parts.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Bits' is informal, mostly British, slang for the genitals.

entries.clue: Stokes notices Carson's beginning to spin deliveries (1-8)

indicatorNotes.beginning: take the first letter of each name
indicatorNotes.to spin: the letters are spun round into a new order

annotation.surface: Cricket commentary: England's Ben Stokes spots a bowler named Carson starting to bowl spin.
annotation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes is an England cricketer and a delivery is a ball bowled, so everything says cricket. The answer is childbirth: a delivery by surgery.
annotation.definitionFit: A C-section, or Caesarean section, is a surgical delivery of a baby.

entries.clue: American on horseback corralling soldiers in city (7)

indicatorNotes.corralling: TONTO pens the soldiers inside, as a corral pens cattle

blocks.note: Tonto, the Native American who rode with the Lone Ranger

annotation.surface: A mounted American rounds up soldiers in a city, like a Western.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' is not US or A here but one particular rider from the old Westerns.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Toronto, capital of Ontario, is one city among many.

entries.clue: Bono's second song reignited loyal hearts (5)

indicatorNotes.hearts: take the middle, the heart, of each word

blocks.note: the middle two letters of song

annotation.surface: U2's Bono releases his second song, which fires up his loyal fans.
annotation.walkthrough: The U2 singer is a decoy: the definition is the other Bono, Sonny, of the duo Sonny & Cher.
annotation.definitionFit: Sonny Bono was the singer who partnered Cher, so Sonny is a Bono.

entries.clue: Priest off the rails with opioid ultimately barred (7)

indicatorNotes.off the rails: PRIEST goes wild, its letters out of order
indicatorNotes.ultimately: 'ultimately' means in the end, so only the word's final letter is used

annotation.surface: A priest who went off the rails on opioids has been banned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barred' looks like banned; it means marked with bars, as a zebra is.
annotation.definitionFit: Barred means marked with bands or stripes, so striped.

entries.clue: Juvenile's released at jail (6)

indicatorNotes.released: AT is let out of the word

annotation.surface: A young offender has been released from jail.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface ends on freedom and the answer means the opposite: to shut someone in.
annotation.definitionFit: To immure is to wall someone up or imprison them.

entries.clue: Came across ducks imitating person (2-3)

blocks.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, so two ducks are OO

annotation.surface: Someone came across ducks mimicking a human.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Me-too' is the adjective for a copycat, so 'imitating person' is a fair match.
annotation.definitionFit: A me-too person copies what others do or have.

entries.clue: Gentle entertainment at river, lying around eating tree nuts (8)

indicatorNotes.lying around: the pair turns round, reading backwards
indicatorNotes.eating: the reversed pair takes the tree letters inside
indicatorNotes.nuts: TREE goes crazy, its letters jumbled

annotation.surface: A pleasant afternoon by the river, lying about eating nuts from the trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tree nuts' looks like a food group; 'nuts' is the anagram signal working on TREE.
annotation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light opera, gentler fare than grand opera.

entries.clue: Theatre taking up a lot of time? (5)

indicatorNotes.taking up: in a down clue, the letters are read upwards

annotation.surface: A complaint that going to the theatre takes up a lot of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' in the sense of a field of action, as in a theatre of war.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre of activity is an arena, a place where things are fought out.

entries.clue: Lied about where cheese comes from? (4)

annotation.surface: Someone lied about where the cheese came from.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a deli is one place cheese comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: A deli, or delicatessen, sells cheese, cold meats and other fine foods.

entries.clue: Strong and popular type of pain relief drug (7)

blocks.note: TENS, a machine that eases pain with small electrical pulses

annotation.surface: An advert for a strong, best-selling painkiller.
annotation.walkthrough: TENS is transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, a device often used in labour.
annotation.definitionFit: Intense means strong or extreme, as in intense heat.

entries.clue: Coot's positive universities can provide stimulation (7)

blocks.note: U = university, plus the LSE, the London School of Economics

annotation.surface: The setter Coot is confident that universities can be stimulating.
annotation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves so the clue can use I or I'M; here Coot's = Coot is.
annotation.definitionFit: An impulse is a stimulus, a force that drives something into motion.

entries.clue: Environmentally conscious film involves no finance expert (9)

indicatorNotes.involves: ECO and MIST wrap round NO, taking it in

blocks.note: a film = a thin haze or coating, such as mist

annotation.surface: A green documentary features no financial experts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; it is a thin layer, like mist on a window.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: economists study money, markets and trade, so they count as finance experts.

entries.clue: Histrionics from a mardy bum not unknown (5)

indicatorNotes.bum: bum = bad, faulty, so the letters are broken up
indicatorNotes.not: 'not' negates the word after it, so the unknown Y is left out of the fodder

blocks.note: y is an algebraic unknown, removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: A tantrum from a sulky layabout, nothing unusual there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mardy' is Northern English for sulky, and 'Mardy Bum' is an Arctic Monkeys song.
annotation.definitionFit: Histrionics are over-the-top emotional displays, which is drama.
